newsitem.title: USA: Some Wal-Mart stores serving McDonald's meals at check-out.
newsitem.headline: Some Wal-Mart stores serving McDonald's meals at check-out.

text.p: Another "impulse" offering is being added to the checkout lines at about 35 Wal-Mart stores across the country -- McDonald's Extra Value Meals.

In addition to candy, gum, breath mints, horoscope books and magazines, customers can buy the Extra Value Meals -- consisting of a sandwich, french fries and a drink -- and pay for them at the Wal-Mart checkout.
"We are looking for additional ways that we can give added convenience to our customers," Chuck Scott, McDonald's assistant vice president for restaurant development, said in a telephone interview.
With the "check-through" programme, customers don't even have to leave the checkout line to get their food. It is delivered to them before they leave the store.

Under an alliance between Oak Brook, Ill.-based McDonald's Corp. and Bentonville, Ark.-based Wal-Mart Stores Inc., McDonald's already has restaurants inside of more than 700 Wal-Mart stores across the country. At this point, the check-through programme involves only 35 of the sites.

The check-through programme began in Sacramento, Calif., nearly two years ago and has spread to various sites across the country since then. While the programme remains a test, more store sites are being considered, Scott said.
"If it's something that works for customers and franchisees, we'd be looking to expand it," he added.
McDonald's stock rose 75 cents to $53.25, while Wal-Mart gained $1.56 to $38.56 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
